## Parent

#121 — spec: Expected-set entry resolves its skill files

## What to build

The toolkit-setup procedure and its integration suite read the enumerator's skill-file facts instead of re-deriving what the Expected set contains. The procedure stops carrying its own dialect for expected names and per-variant instruction files, and the suite asserts the shipped contract through the enumerator's interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The toolkit-setup integration suite asserts the enumerator's skill-file facts for the repo tree — every entry resolves all its skill files, file order is deterministic, and the entry order guarantee still holds — with no reference to the entry-level resolution status.
- [ ] The toolkit-setup procedure instructs the agent to read the enumerated facts (which entries exist, which files each owns, which are agent definitions) rather than re-deriving expected names and per-variant files from the lock files and directory scan.
- [ ] The procedure still reports the same outcomes for a healthy checkout: every shared entry present, exactly one router `SKILL.md` per coupled skill, runtime instruction files present, codex agent links verified, principles linked.
- [ ] The setup flow's report format is unchanged, and the suite passes in a partially provisioned checkout.

## Blocked by

- #122 — Expected-set entry resolves its skill files (expand).
title: Toolkit-setup reads skill files instead of re-deriving the Expected set
